bodyMarkdown:
## Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary with Our Salary to Hourly Rate Calculator Australia

If you are an employee or contractor in Australia, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual pay is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, or checking your entitlements. Our [salary to hourly rate calculator australia] is designed to give you a quick estimate of your gross annual salary, fortnightly pay, tax, and superannuation based on a standard 38-hour working week. This article explains the formula, the assumptions we use, and how casual loading and super are handled.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The core calculation is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours worked per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours every week, the formula becomes:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. The calculator also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly pay × 2) to help with budgeting.

### When We Assume 38 Hours per Week

Under the Fair Work Act, the standard full-time week is 38 hours. Our calculator uses this as the default. If you work fewer or more hours, you can adjust the hours per week field. However, the annual figure is always based on the hours you enter multiplied by 52 weeks. This is a simple estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees in Australia are entitled to a 25% loading on their base hourly rate under most awards and the National Minimum Wage. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays. Our calculator includes a checkbox that adds 25% casual loading to the base rate you enter. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator applies it automatically. For example, if the base rate is $26.44 (the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026), checking the casual loading box gives a casual rate of $33.05 per hour. The annual gross and fortnightly figures then reflect this loaded rate.

### Distinguishing the National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Our calculator is not a substitute for checking your specific award. For award rates, refer to the [pay guides] or [reference tables] on our site. The calculator uses the rate you enter, which should be your base hourly rate under your award or agreement (excluding casual loading if you are casual).

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must pay superannuation contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Our calculator estimates super as 12% of your gross annual pay, shown separately. For example, if your annual gross is $59,280, the estimated super is $7,113.60. Note that super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution by your employer. The calculator does not account for salary sacrifice or personal contributions.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

The calculator deducts tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. The tax estimate is for a resident individual claiming the full tax-free threshold. If you have a spouse, children, or other deductions, your actual tax may differ.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. The calculator shows your fortnightly gross pay (weekly pay × 2) and the estimated tax and super for that period. This helps you compare with job offers or plan your budget. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,004.90 (based on the minimum wage), your fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay will be lower.

### Using the Calculator for Different Scenarios

Our [salary to hourly rate calculator australia] is versatile. You can:
- Enter your hourly rate to see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures.
- Check the casual loading box if you are a casual employee.
- Adjust hours per week if you work part-time or overtime.
- See the estimated super paid on top.

The calculator is not a substitute for professional advice. For specific questions about your pay, contact the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Australian Taxation Office.

### Important Limitations

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
